correctness.rationale: For each residue \(r\) modulo odd \(a\), represent with \(t=y+3z\) and minimize its coin coefficient as \(c(t)=2(t-\lfloor t/3\rfloor)\). Every residue corresponds to a unique \(t\in[0,a-1]\), and the monotonicity of \(c\) proves the exact Apéry threshold. The two alternating-parity threshold sequences yield a row decomposition: singleton odd gaps and a unique even terminal interval. Exact row multiplicities are the increments of \(c\). Genus minus total even-terminal-gap length gives the three quadratic isolated-gap expressions. The boundary cases \(a=3\), row transitions, and conductor are covered. A separate finite Dijkstra/dynamic-programming comparison verifies all cases for odd \(a\le251\), without replacing the proof.

originality.rationale: The target is the complete maximal-consecutive-gap distribution, not known Apéry representatives, Frobenius number, genus, minimal binomial presentations, or two-generator gap spectra. The 2023 same-family primary works were inspected and their membership information is explicitly credited. The new period-three support and exact two-or-zero multiplicities are not asserted there. An implicit equivalent of the histogram in a prior source remains a real priority risk and was not ruled out by search absence.
residual_risks: Because prior Apéry formulas compute every gap in the same family, a published implicit evaluation of the same full histogram cannot be excluded by targeted checks.
The general two-generator isolated-gap literature was compared using its domain and indexed statements, not exhaustively for all possible reductions.
The mathematical literature may contain unindexed or differently named equivalent explicit enumerations.

value.rationale: The complete maximal-consecutive-gap histogram is a natural invariant of numerical-semigroup holes. The theorem gives an infinite odd-parameter family with a sparse exact support: every longer gap run occurs precisely twice or is absent according to a period-three law, while isolated gaps have a quadratic quasipolynomial. This locates structural gap-clustering information not captured by the usual Frobenius number or genus and supplies a reproducible closed classification rather than arbitrary small-parameter enumeration. The fact that its Apéry input is known is credited.
